clinician.final_diagnosis: The histopathology results from a skin biopsy indicated psoriasiform secondary syphilis
clinician.trajectory_summary: A 63-year-old man with a 30-year history of psoriasis and well-controlled HIV presented with recurrent generalized scaly erythema. A skin biopsy revealed plasma cell infiltration in the superficial dermis and perivascular areas, with a roughly normal epidermis. The histopathology diagnosis was psoriasiform secondary syphilis. Serological tests confirmed syphilis with positive TPPA and a TRUST titre of 1:2048. Treatment with 2.4 million weekly units of benzathine penicillin intramuscularly for 3 consecutive weeks was initiated, leading to a significant diminution of lesions, although some psoriatic scaly erythema and plaques remained.

key_supporting_evidence.claim: Patient presented with recurrent episodes of generalised scaly erythema, with multiple erythematous and hyperpigmented patches, mostly dark red patches and a few scales on the surface.
Patient has a 30-year history of psoriasis and well-controlled HIV infection.
Skin biopsy showed additional plasma cell infiltration of the superficial dermis and perivascular areas, and the epidermis was roughly normal with individual infiltrating cells.
The overall histopathology diagnosis from the skin biopsy was psoriasiform secondary syphilis.
Serological tests yielded positive TPPA results and a TRUST titre of 1:2048.
Treatment was started with 2.4 million weekly units of benzathine penicillin administered intramuscularly for 3 consecutive weeks.
After treatment, the lesions diminished significantly, though psoriatic scaly erythema and plaques remained on the abdomen and waist.
